_README: PIXELTOSSA art manifest. This file is the ONLY thing that decides whether a visual
element is a sprite or a procedural drawing. Game.gd never names a PNG.
1. author the art at 640x360 density (see _AUTHORING below)
2. save it into the matching Assets/ folder
3. add a line here, keyed by the seam key
4. run the game - that element is now a sprite; delete the line to go back
DESIGN VARIANTS. Resources/art_variants/<set>.<option>.json is a SECOND manifest of the
same shape, laid over this one by art_boot: every key it names replaces the sprite here
and every key it does not name is left alone. That is the whole variant system - see the
F9 panel (THE LOOK) or --variant <set>:<option>. Option 0 of each set is what ships and
has no file, so a release build reads this manifest and nothing else.
A key with no line here draws procedurally. A line whose file is missing logs one
warning and falls back, so you can reserve a key before the art exists. Keys
beginning with _ are documentation and are skipped.
TO SEE THE LIVE KEY LIST, run the game with:  --artreport
It prints every key the running session actually reached, marked [sprite] or [proc].
That list is generated from the code, so it can never go stale the way this comment
can. The _KEYS block below is a convenience copy.

_AUTHORING.canvas: 640x360 is the art's pixel density; the game's coordinate space stays 1280x720
_AUTHORING.scale: 1 art pixel is drawn as a 2x2 screen block (ART_PIXEL = 2), no resampling
_AUTHORING.rule: author at 1/2 the screen size you want, e.g. a 24px-wide ball on screen = 12px of art
_AUTHORING.import: PNG, lossless, no mipmaps, nearest filter - project.godot's importer_defaults does this
_AUTHORING.tint: the ROUND props (ball, egg, ring), hands and gear are drawn through the game's colour as a TINT, so author those WHITE. Club, knife, torch and chainsaw carry their own painted palettes and never see the tint.
_AUTHORING.pivot: [0.5,0.5] is the centre; [0.5,1.0] pins the bottom edge to the draw position. For a spinning prop the pivot is NOT the centre - it is the point the game rotates the shape about, derived from the drawing constants rather than eyeballed.
_AUTHORING.scale_field: optional multiplier if the art is authored bigger or smaller than its slot

_DENSITY_CHANGED: See the PIXEL-ART RENDER SEAM region in Game.gd for the measurement behind it. Short
version: the figure survives a 4x downsample and the HUD text does not.
THE FOUR PROPS THE PREP PASS REGISTERED (ball, ring, club, knife) WERE UNREGISTERED
HERE IN THE SAME COMMIT, and this is the trap worth naming: changing ART_PIXEL cannot
rescale a PNG. Those files were authored for the old density - a 6x6 ball - so after
the switch they would simply have drawn at half the size they used to, which looks
like a bug in the seam and is not. They are being redrawn at 640x360 density.
The old files are still in Assets/Props/ and are inert until a line below names them.

_KEYS.prop/*: ball egg ring club knife torch chainsaw  (Assets/Props/, round ones tinted, all rotated)
_KEYS.char/*: head head_back hat_top glasses helmet boot hand_open hand_closed glove_open glove_closed
_KEYS.bg/*: backyard street_corner small_theatre the_circus championship world_arena midnight_show
_KEYS.ui/*: keycap card_skill card_trick gear_glasses gear_pie gear_gloves ...

_LIVE: Below are the real, registered sprites. Everything else is still drawn by code.
THE SEVEN PROPS, generated by scripts/pixelise_prop.py from --propref renders of the
game's own drawing. Not generated by PixelLab: its smallest canvas is 1024 pixels of
area and every prop here is under it (a ball is 11x11 = 121, a club 6x32 = 192, even
the chainsaw at 21x48 is 1008). Deriving them from TOSSA's real silhouette is also
simply better - a prop is on screen at all times and the player reads its shape to
catch it, so it is the last thing that should be reinterpreted.
EVERY PIVOT BELOW WAS MEASURED, NOT CHOSEN, and three of them are not the centre.
The pivot is the point the game ROTATES the shape about; get it wrong and the prop
orbits a point instead of spinning about it. The club's 0.558 matches what the prep
pass derived by hand. The knife's does NOT: measurement says 0.624 where the hand
derivation said 0.663, because the drawn span is 41.3 local units and the comment it
came from claims 39.2. The torch and chainsaw are off-centre HORIZONTALLY too (0.441,
0.438) because those props are not symmetric about their grip. Re-measure with
--propref rather than editing these by eye.
Delete any line to send that prop back to procedural. Run with --procart to A/B all.
